meta.title: Ep 4 - Hội An to Da Nang, Central Vietnam | Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary | Han Market | Dragon Bridge night view
meta.description:
In this video you will see our journey from Hội An to Da Nang which is part of Central Vietnam. In between we visited Historical landmarks in Vietnam and tourist destinations too.

In case you haven't watched the previous episodes of Vietnam, here is the link of playlist

https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLxHSKe-bOElw9DVfzDTNPDyDd3aICK4Ld 

Spices website link - https://spice2nuts.com/

Gadgets we use for Visa2explore & Harish Bali Travels.
Sony A 7 111 camera: https://amzn.to/4clE2zI
Z -90 Sony: https://amzn.to/3SO8T10
Go pro Hero 12: https://amzn.to/46GULw6
IPhone 15 Pro: https://amzn.to/3YJgr8Y

For Background Music, we use “Epidemic Sound” in our videos. You can use it from the link below.

https://www.epidemicsound.com/referral/ujnsd6

Date of Journey - 8th April 2025

Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary - It is a famous UNESCO World Heritage Site in Central Vietnam which showcase the ancient Champa civilization and its Hindu temples. 
These ruined Hindu temples are abandoned as of now and these Hindu temples were constructed in between the 4th and the 13th century by the Kings of Champa. Inside there is a museum too which also explains the history of this place.
There is also a dance performance done by the locals which shows how the Champa civilization used to celebrate festivals.

Dance timing Monday to Saturday:
Morning - 9:45 AM, 10:30 AM, 11:15 AM
Afternoon - 2:00 PM

Entry Ticket: VND - 1,50,000
INR - 510 (Approx)

Sangha Vegetarian Restaurant - We had Vietnamese food for lunch here.
Nấm Sốt Bơ Tỏi: 
VND - 1,15,000
INR - 380 (Approx)

Nấm Nấu Trấi Dứa:
VND - 1,25,000
INR - 410 (Approx)

Han River - Han River is a major waterway that flows through the heart of Da Nang. It is famous for its vibrant city life, scenic beauty, and iconic bridges. 

Han Market - It is one of the famous and old markets of Da Nang. A wide range of goods, including fashion, souvenirs, and local specialties can be seen here. Locals and tourists both can find everything here like clothing and accessories to dried foods and unique handicrafts. 

Dragon Bridge - It is one of the famous Bridges in Han River Da Nang, which can "breathe" fire and water, adding to the city's unique charm. This is also one of the main tourist attractions at night time.

After this we ended our day. Hope you enjoyed the video.

Sir, you will enjoy William Dalrymple’s books . He is a world renowned historian living in Delhi. One of his books The Golden Road covers the spread of Buddhist and Hindu cultures in South East Asia.  It also talks about Champa and the influence of the dynasties in South India- the Pallavas, Cholas, and Chalukya. The great Khamir empire whose capital city was called Yashodharapura now known as Angkor which also has the world’s largest Hindu temple complex AngkorWat - present day Cambodia. 
The world Angkor comes from Nokor in Khamir which is the root of nagar in Sanskrit. Khamir kings were Hindus .
You will absolutely have an unbelievable experience in covering Angkor Wat. - it takes several days to cover such a massive complex.
Hope reading Dalrymple’s books will inspire you to explore regions and stories not yet explored by you.

comments.text:
:: Honest Review:: Harish sir I hope you read the below content full.
Waste of 24min. Information told already available over internet or other YouTube channels. Question is how is this video different from others? If a dish is shown never ever exact name told so how will others know that it should be or shouldn't be ordered. You too should rate food based on your taste buds. No point then showing clip of you tasting food. Again it's useless to have such part included and stretch the videos. 
I have been an appreciator of your work on how you go to undiscovered places of India and document its heritage , culture, people to be used and referred by future generations. It seems the charm and cause which use to appear in earlier videos is slowly vanishing. If you record popular places, museums, etc in today's world every YouTubers are doing. I believe you shouldn't yourself just to be YouTuber like other thousands of channels. After watching this video I can't stop writing to you. To be honest from experience perspective I see with such contents even the channel growth will get lost amongst others.
Wearing a blunt consumer-hat I tell you the latest videos are not worth of content quality so why should I spend my 30-40 min of Sunday for your channel.
Love and respect from,
- Sandy (West Bengal)
